extracted.intended_audience: mathematics faculty, instructors, and department curriculum planners (especially those responsible for undergraduate programs and first/second-year courses)
extracted.subtask_description: Provide precise definitions and frameworks for 'mathematical maturity' and 'mathematical proficiency' to guide teaching, course design, and departmental discussion for undergraduate mathematics. The page presents psychological domains, the five-strand model, and MAA/CUPM recommendations with practical steps to implement them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual (cognitive) domain
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellectual, or cognitive, domain regards knowledge and understanding of concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a three-domain framing of mathematical maturity. Use this label to distinguish students who 'know the math' (conceptual understanding) from those who struggle with other domains. Can be refined by the first two strands (conceptual understanding and procedural fluency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral (enactive) domain
rubrics_metrics.description: The behavioral, or enactive, domain regards the practices and actions with which we apply or develop that knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers habits, practices, and strategies (e.g., problem solving persistence, method choice). Refined by strands such as strategic competence and adaptive reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional (affective) domain
rubrics_metrics.description: The emotional, or affective, domain regards how we feel about our knowledge and our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses productive disposition: whether students see mathematics as sensible, useful, worthwhile and believe in diligence and their own efficacy. Important for explaining differences where students have skills but low confidence or persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual understanding (five-strand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehension of mathematical concepts, operations, and relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the five strands of mathematical proficiency. Example: student can compute a derivative but cannot use it to find the equation of a tangent line — shows procedural skill but lacking conceptual understanding. Maps to the intellectual/cognitive domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural fluency (five-strand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in carrying out procedures flexibly, accurately, efficiently, and appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the five strands. Procedural fluency combined with conceptual understanding enables broader competence. Example: student can compute derivatives and explain derivations (e.g., quadratic formula) but may still fail at multistep modeling problems if strategic competence is weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic competence (five-strand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to formulate, represent, and solve mathematical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the five strands; refines the behavioral/enactive domain. Example: struggling with multistep modeling (max/min) indicates weaker strategic competence despite procedural / conceptual ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive reasoning (five-strand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity for logical thought, reflection, explanation, and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the five strands; connects to behavioral practices of justification and the intellectual domain of reasoning and explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productive disposition (five-strand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Habitual inclination to see mathematics as sensible, useful, and worthwhile, coupled with a belief in diligence and one’s own efficacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the five strands aligned with the emotional/affective domain. Example: students with negative views of mathematics may lack persistence and self-efficacy needed to succeed even if they possess conceptual or procedural skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — precise problem statement & logical reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: State problems carefully, articulate assumptions, understand the importance of precise definition, and reason logically to conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From MAA CUPM Curriculum Guide (Cognitive Recommendation 1). Programs should include activities that train careful problem formulation, assumption articulation, precision in definitions, and logical reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — modeling complex situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and model essential features of a complex situation, modify models as necessary for tractability, and draw useful conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages training in abstraction and pragmatic model modification; part of the CUPM list of desired cognitive skills for majors.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — deduce general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce general principles from particular instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports pattern recognition and generalization abilities; included in CUPM Cognitive Recommendation 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — use multiple perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and compare analytical, visual, and numerical perspectives in exploring mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages fluency across representations (algebraic, geometric, numerical, graphical) and comparison between them; included in CUPM guidance for majors.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — assess solutions and experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the correctness of solutions, create and explore examples, carry out mathematical experiments, and devise and test conjectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes validation, example-construction, experimentation, and the conjecture-testing cycle as curricular goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — recognize and make rigorous arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and make mathematically rigorous arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit focus on proof, justification, and rigor appropriate to advanced undergraduate-level work.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — read mathematics with understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Read mathematics with understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets the skill of comprehending mathematical texts and extracting meaning from formal exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — communicate mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate mathematical ideas clearly and coherently both verbally and in writing to audiences of varying mathematical sophistication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes both oral and written communication tailored to diverse audiences; part of core cognitive recommendations for majors.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — approach with curiosity and persistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach mathematical problems with curiosity and creativity and persist in the face of difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages attitudes of curiosity, creativity, and perseverance as curricular outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Cognitive Recommendation — creative and self-sufficient work
rubrics_metrics.description: Work creatively and self-sufficiently with mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fosters independent mathematical thought and creative problem solving in majors.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Content Recommendation — continuous and discrete perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key ideas from complementary points of view: continuous and discrete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four complementary content-perspective recommendations (Content Recommendation 6) advising majors' curricula to expose students to multiple facets of mathematical ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Content Recommendation — algebraic and geometric perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key ideas from complementary points of view: algebraic and geometric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages teaching that connects algebraic and geometric viewpoints for deeper understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Content Recommendation — deterministic and stochastic perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key ideas from complementary points of view: deterministic and stochastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urges inclusion of both deterministic and probabilistic/stochastic viewpoints in presenting key ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: CUPM Content Recommendation — exact and approximate perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key ideas from complementary points of view: exact and approximate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends balancing exact theoretical methods with approximate and numerical approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental practice — present frameworks in faculty seminar
rubrics_metrics.description: Have two or three faculty jointly present these frameworks/definitions of proficiency during a department seminar or colloquium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical step to build shared language. Use joint presentations to introduce three-domain, five-strand, and CUPM language to faculty for common understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental practice — review course structure against frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather a team of faculty to review the structure and content of a course for first-year students using the three domain and five strand model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask which domains/strands are targeted by assignments or activities and which may be unintentionally omitted. Use this as a diagnostic to redesign course elements to cover missing strands/domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental practice — major-level goal alignment exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a similar exercise for a major level course or sequence using MAA CUPM language to check which goals are being trained explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If particular CUPM goals are not treated in a course, identify other required courses that provide opportunities to develop those goals; helps curricular mapping for majors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental practice — student activity/survey using framework language
rubrics_metrics.description: Design a short activity/survey for students based on this language to have them identify class activities that helped develop particular domains/strands/goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use student feedback from the activity/survey as data for faculty discussion at department meetings to inform course design and evidence of student development.
